newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FOCUS-J.Martins bids for Portugal's Vidago.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-J.Martins bids for Portugal's Vidago.

text.p: Portugal's second biggest retailer Jeronimo Martins on Tuesday formally announced a bid for the country's leading sparkling water supplier Vidago, valuing it at 15.8 billion escudos ($104 million).

The preliminary announcement of the public offer to buy at 4,300 escudos a share, published in Publico newspaper, said the bid was conditional on Vidago's shareholders selling at least 90 percent of the company's 3.7 billion escudos capital.
After saying on Saturday it would bid for Vidago, Jeronimo Martins' offer was at the upper end of analysts expectations of around 4,000 escudos a share.
Analysts said Jeronimo Martins wanted to buy Vidago because the market for sparkling water was growing, but newspapers suggested it might sell Vidago's hotel interests.

Trade in Unicer shares was briefly suspended by Lisbon bourse authorities on Tuesday after Diario Economico newspaper reported the drinks group could launch a counter-bid for Vidago. Trade in Unicer shares resumed after the company denied this to bourse authorities.

Diario Economico quoted a source close to Unicer, which distributes beer, mineral water, wine and juices, as saying his company was interested in acquiring Vidago, even though it believed the price bid by Jeronimo Martins was too high.
If a company decided to make a counter-offer for Vidago, it would have to offer a price that was at least five percent higher than the previous bid, according to Portuguese law.
The Financial Markets Committee (CMVM) on Tuesday ended a 24-hour suspension in trade in Vidago shares on the Lisbon bourse.
As trading in the shares resumed, Vidago surged and stood 995 escudos up in early afternoon trade at 4,200.
Jeronimo Martins shares stood at 14,030 escudos, up 10, in volume of 400 shares.
